appraisal_events.evidence: 'pourquoi ne viendriez-vous pas dîner chez moi ?' ... 'Vendredi vous ne seriez pas libre, en petit comité ? ... Il y aura la princesse de Parme qui est charmante ; d'abord je ne vous inviterais pas si ce n'était pas pour rencontrer des gens agréables.' The narrator recalls that entering the Guermantes salon had been 'interdit,' with 'la barrière où finit le réel' between himself and it.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Guermantes moves from a passing remark to a specific, intimate dinner invitation naming a distinguished fellow guest, and the narrator recognizes this as crossing the very barrier that had long sealed the Guermantes salon off from him, reading it as a genuine welcome rather than a perfunctory courtesy extended to an outsider.

status_effects.explanation: Mme de Guermantes personally and explicitly invites him to a select 'petit comité' dinner alongside the princesse de Parme, a direct, spoken mark of favor witnessed within the scene itself.
The narrator explicitly frames the Guermantes salon as long forbidden to him, and this invitation crosses that very boundary, admitting him into a world he had thought sealed off.
